title: The system: a podcast hosting platform, every box labelled with its number
caption: Read the sub-labels: 0.1 uploads/s, 4.5 TB/day, 24k polls/s and 50 Gbps each pick a different component.

steps.text: Six assumptions drive everything: 70 000 active shows, one episode a week each, 60 MB per episode, 10 M listeners, one download per listener a day, 10 subscribed feeds polled hourly. Peak = 5× average (Monday morning).
Writes: 70 000 ÷ 7 = 10 000 episodes/day ÷ 1e5 s ≈ 0.1 uploads/s. Tiny: one small Upload API. Transcoding takes minutes, so it goes through a queue and the upload returns at once.

Bytes: the original plus 3 lower bitrates ≈ 150 MB per episode, so 1.5 TB/day, ×3 replicas = 4.5 TB/day, about 1.6 PB a year. That says object storage. The episode row (a few KB) is 10k rows/day: one relational primary.

RSS: 10 M × 10 feeds × 24 polls = 2.4 B/day ≈ 24 000 polls/s. Feeds change about once a week, so ~99% are cache hits, and all 70 000 feeds × 50 KB ≈ 3.5 GB fit in one cache node. The builder and the DB see ~240/s.
Downloads: 10 M/day ÷ 1e5 s = 100/s. Egress: 100 × 60 MB × 8 ≈ 50 Gbps on average and 240 Gbps at the 5× peak. Only a CDN serves that; the audio store sees misses only.
Analytics: one access-log event per download, 100/s (500/s at peak) × 200 B ≈ 2 GB/day. A log plus an aggregator that dedupes repeat fetches gives creators their counts minutes later.

scenarios.name: Monday 7 am peak
scenarios.summary: New episodes land Sunday night and auto-download for the commute: downloads go 5×, and every new file starts cold at every CDN edge.

steps.text: Shows publish overnight. Within an hour every app's poll sees the new item and queues an auto-download.
Downloads jump from 100/s to 500/s: 500 × 60 MB × 8 ≈ 240 Gbps, spread over the CDN's edges.
Each new episode is a cold object, so its first request at each edge misses. Misses are collapsed per region, and the audio store sees one fetch per episode per region, not one per listener.
The log takes 500 events/s easily; the aggregator falls a few minutes behind and catches up by mid-morning. Stats being late is fine; downloads failing is not.

scenarios.name: Feed cache down
scenarios.summary: 24k polls/s fall through to the builder and the DB, which were sized for 240/s. Shed and answer cheaply until a new node warms.

steps.text: Polls fall through: 24 000 builds/s, each reading the DB. That is 100× what the builder was sized for and above one primary's ~10k reads/s.
Degrade: answer 304 Not Modified from the feed's last-updated time (one cheap indexed read) and shed the rest with 503 + Retry-After. An app that misses one hourly poll just tries next hour.
A replacement node warms by rebuilding all 70 000 feeds: at ~1 000 builds/s that is about 70 s. Then the builder is back to ~240/s.

scenarios.name: New bitrate rollout
scenarios.summary: Adding a 48 kbps file for low-bandwidth listeners means re-transcoding the whole back catalogue: estimate CPU and storage before saying yes.

steps.text: Product wants a 48 kbps rendition. The back catalogue is about 3 M episodes, so 3 M backfill jobs are queued.
At ~1 CPU-minute per episode that is 3 M CPU-minutes ≈ 50 000 CPU-hours: 300 cores for about a week.
Storage: 1 h at 48 kbps ≈ 20 MB, so 3 M × 20 MB × 3 replicas ≈ 180 TB, about six weeks of normal growth.
Run the backfill at low priority in its own queue so Monday's new uploads still transcode in minutes; each episode row gains the new file when it is done.
